written_by: Claude Code, for Ryan Saleh to check
notes: Business administration for Explore (spec 21), batch 2. Every name and description is in Stackd's own words; nothing is copied from UC's page. C-ID numbers, the template number and revision, the degree name, the unit totals and the campus major names are copied exactly. UC pathway: the Business Administration Transfer Pathway page on admission.universityofcalifornia.edu (it states no term or year; academic_year is the year it was checked). TMC: template #2006, the PDF in source_url. A pick-one row lists the template's choices that have a C-ID number; choices with no C-ID number are in its description, because an option must have one. Topics in both pathways (Counts for both): financial-accounting, managerial-accounting, microeconomics, macroeconomics, statistics. Intro to business isn't shared: the template's row also accepts business communication, which UC doesn't ask for, so marking that row done wouldn't always mean UC's course is done. Both rows point at each other in their descriptions. Calculus is kept apart too: UC asks for a year, the template for one math course. Business law is Cal State only. Check every row against its source, delete each todo once confirmed, fill in retrieved_at on both pathways, then run: npm run import -- data/raw/explore/business-administration.json --dry-run

requirements.name: Microeconomics
requirements.description: How people and businesses make choices about prices and money.

requirements.name: Macroeconomics
requirements.description: How a whole economy works: growth, jobs, inflation and policy.

requirements.name: Calculus, a full year
requirements.description: A year-long single-variable calculus sequence. Take the STEM version if you can; some campuses accept a non-STEM version, so check yours. Cal State's degree asks for one math course instead.

requirements.name: Intro to business
requirements.description: A survey of how businesses run. It should cover finance. In Cal State's degree this is one of two choices, so pick intro to business there and it works for UC too.

requirements.name: Financial accounting
requirements.description: How a business records its money and reports it to people outside the company.
